Autumn is a big moment for sports fans, and ESPN recently rolled out a major upgrade for its tvOS and iOS app users: 4K HDR streaming.

ESPN's streaming service now supports 4K HDR, with the tvOS and iOS apps being the first to receive support.

Over the past few weeks, ESPN has been rolling out major upgrades to its tvOS and iOS apps.

The streaming service now offers 4K HDR picture quality for its top programming, including live NFL, NBA, and NHL events.

This week, ESPN and ESPN2 will become the first U.S. channels to broadcast live in 4K HDR, delivering a sharper picture to fans during one of the most action-packed stretches on the sports calendar. That includes all ESPN-produced Monday Night Football, NBA, and NHL games, as well as select college football and US Open telecasts, plus marquee live events like Super Bowl LXI. The upgrade brings crisper edges, more vivid colours, and smoother motion — all critical for elevating the sports viewing experience with richer, more lifelike visuals. The ESPN app will be first to support the new experience on iOS and tvOS, before expanding to other connected TV platforms later, with Disney+ in the U.S. also offering support for ESPN Unlimited subscribers.

When browsing the ESPN app, you'll notice a new '4K HDR' label appearing next to content that supports the high-quality video stream.

As long as you have a stable internet connection at home or on the go, 4K HDR will deliver more vivid, sharper, and higher-quality visuals for your favourite sports content.

If you're a sports fan considering picking up an Apple TV 4K for the first time, you may want to hold off. A new Apple TV model is reportedly on the way.

Now that ESPN has rolled out 4K HDR content, have you checked it out? How does it look? Let us know in the comments.
